subject.title: [Feature]: Inline agent widgets in web chat via client-capability-gated tools

question: Should OpenClaw add a generic `requiredClientCaps` tool-availability contract for web-only inline widget tools, with Canvas owning the first `show_widget` implementation?
rationale: The issue proposes a new gateway-to-tool API seam plus model-authored markup rendering; repository policy supports plugin API extensions when needed but requires maintainer direction for core/plugin boundaries and security-sensitive surfaces.

options.title: Design the generic capability seam
options.body: Accept the core/SDK capability-gating work as a maintainer-sponsored design task and keep the actual widget renderer owned by Canvas/plugin code.

options.title: Prototype outside core first
options.body: Require a ClawHub or local plugin prototype to prove the exact missing API before adding SDK or gateway surface area.

options.title: Defer rich widgets
options.body: Keep the issue open but unscheduled until web chat embed security and native-client rendering adoption goals are clearer.

recommendation.title: Design the generic capability seam
recommendation.body: Accept the core/SDK capability-gating work as a maintainer-sponsored design task and keep the actual widget renderer owned by Canvas/plugin code.

likelyOwner.reason: The prior rich-output/embed work is the closest current implementation boundary for deciding whether the next step belongs in core, SDK, or Canvas/plugin code.
